rims.statement: approved reference = 5-6 micrographs; 6 independent incoming micrographs; verdict rests on M2060; out-of-family prevalence 1/6 (95% CI 0-64%)
68% of the excess high-Z objects are < 0.7 µm and the excess ratio peaks at the 0.36 µm detection floor (2.3×): the anomalous population is truncated by the pixel size.
deviation still outside the approved local band at the start of the 698 µm captured section
the surviving deviation is in the high-Z phase, whose chemistry is not measured: BSE alone cannot separate a finer additive from a different lower-Z phase.
deviation still outside the approved local band at the end of the 524 µm captured section
Additive density: adjacent-tile variance 1.9× the short-range prediction (95% CI 1.1-4.2); variogram still rising at 400 µm (structure larger than the longest coherent capture)
Porosity: adjacent-tile variance 3.6× the short-range prediction (95% CI 2.0-7.8); variogram range ≈ 175 µm

actions.title: Repeat M2060 under the approved acquisition settings
evidence: verdict changes without M2060 (REJECT → ACCEPT, p = 0.45)
6 acquisition metrics differ from the approved micrographs
actions.rationale: The only test that separates acquisition from material for the decision-driving evidence. Tested perturbations explain little, but kV / working distance / dwell were never varied; new fields elsewhere would confound both.

actions.title: Higher magnification + low-kV BSE on M2060 fines
evidence: 68% of excess objects < 0.7 µm; excess ratio 2.3× at the 0.36 µm detection floor
actions.rationale: The anomalous population is cut off by the pixel size. A wider field only adds more truncated counts; a finer pixel (≤ 10 nm) resolves the population, and low kV suppresses the sub-surface signal that makes fines look dim.

actions.title: Paired EDS: M2060 fines vs approved additive
evidence: fine objects at the dim end of the approved BSE range (u = 0.77)
actions.rationale: BSE contrast cannot distinguish a finer specified additive from a different lower-Z phase; no further BSE capture resolves chemistry. This decides supplier attribution.

actions.title: Extend the M2060 mosaic beyond its start
evidence: Additive density outside the approved local band along 95% of the 698 µm section and still outside at the start
actions.rationale: Bounds the anomalous region (local inclusion vs extended zone). More tiles inside the current section are redundant: the deviation is already measured there (z = 6.7).

actions.title: Independent cross-sections from the lot (not adjacent tiles)
evidence: approved reference = 5-6 micrographs; 6 independent incoming micrographs; verdict rests on M2060; out-of-family prevalence 1/6 (95% CI 0-64%)
adjacent tiles are partly redundant for Additive density, Porosity (structure ≥ field scale)
actions.rationale: Answers how much of the lot is affected. More tiles of an anomalous micrograph refine a number that is already decisive; only independent sections constrain prevalence.

actions.title: Extend the M2088 mosaic beyond its end
evidence: Porosity outside the approved local band along 67% of the 524 µm section and still outside at the end
actions.rationale: Bounds the anomalous region (local inclusion vs extended zone). More tiles inside the current section are redundant: the deviation is already measured there (z = 2.6).

actions.title: Porosity: fields spaced ≥ 175 µm instead of adjacent tiles
evidence: deviation inconsistent across fields in M2088
actions.rationale: Fields closer than the correlation range re-measure the same structure; spacing them by at least the range makes each field an approximately independent sample of this KPI.

actions.title: Expand the approved reference (+5 independent micrographs)
actions.rationale: Every envelope is partly baseline-estimation uncertainty; this shrinks all of them, but changes no current flag.
